agent: ministers wave, reader C (the production script's units and constructions), 2026-10-16
question: What each engine method TFH's ai_production_minister.lua and Support.CreateUnit reach about unit types, the build queue and the country answers - which field, filled where and when, counted how - and what CConstructUnitCommand does with each Lua argument

addresses.name: CEU3AI::UpdateSubUnitCounts
addresses.comment: **Fills the three per-type count arrays the production script reads, and nothing else fills them.** `ai` on the stack, `ret 4` at 0x899A04. Its one caller is CAIProductionMinister::DoWork (0x8A2424), which calls it every day in the minister's hour (`(id + 5) % 24`), before the desperation cache and the Lua `ProductionMinister_Tick`. In order: (1) zeroes every entry of DeployedSubUnitCounts (+0xE8), ProductionSubUnitCounts (+0xF8) and TheatreSubUnitNeedCounts (+0x108), as many as the database has types; (2) **production**: for every line of the country's queue (CCountry +0xF40) whose slot 17 (IsMilitary) answers true, for every brigade definition of the line (+0x7C), `production[definition->Type->type_index] += line->Size (+0x40)` - so a line counts each of its brigades once for every unit of its series still to come, building and convoy lines nothing; (3) **deployed**: for every entry of the country's deployments (+0x688) whose slot 8 answers 0x4B4 (a CUnitDeployment; a CBuildingDeployment answers 0x4B7), every brigade of the waiting unit (deployment +0x38, its regiments at +0x38) adds 1 at its definition's (+0x58) type_index; then every brigade of every unit in CCountry +0xBAC adds 1 the same way - one count per brigade, wherever the unit is and whatever it is doing; (4) **theatre**: for every unit agent (+0x40) whose slot 74 answers a unit, that unit's plan_subunit_group_difference (CUnit +0x6C) is added entry by entry, each entry floored at 0 after each addition, the transport_ship type (database +0x88) skipped when every COwnerArea of the country (+0xD30) is landlocked (+0x68 set); (5) hasFilledProdQueue (+0xAA) = 1. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ministers.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x899770-0x899A04: the zeroing loop 0x8997F0-0x89981A over (db+0x20 - db+0x1C)/4; the queue walk 0x899826-0x89986F with `call [vftable+0x44]` and `add [ecx], [esi+0x40]` into [ebx+0xF8]; the deployment walk 0x899874-0x8998CD with `cmp eax,0x4B4` after `call [vftable+0x20]` and `inc [edx+ecx*4]` into [ebx+0xE8]; the units walk 0x8998D2-0x899913 over [esi+0xBAC]; the agent walk 0x899943-0x8999E7 through [vftable+0x128]; `mov byte [ebx+0xAA],1` at 0x8999F1. findRefs --callers: one call, 0x8A2424. A triple scan for disp32 0xE8 and 0xF8 found no other CEU3AI-region writer than the constructor 0x888020 and destructor 0x8885C0 (positive control: it found the two Lua getters at 0x8E8180/0x8E8190). Wrong if a second writer reaches the arrays through a pointer the scan cannot see. **Reader B also has this address as a starting point (0x499770(OwnerAI) in DoWork); the collector should reconcile the name.**

addresses.name: SubUnitTypeGroup
addresses.comment: **Folds a unit type onto the representative type of its group**, answering a type_index. Both arguments in registers, bare `ret`. For definition = database->definitions_begin[typeIndex]: a **ship** (is_ship +0x2E): carrier_size (+0x190) above 0 - the `carrier` type; the heavy_cruiser itself - itself; is_capital (+0x2F) - `battleship`; is_transport (+0x30) or is_sub (+0x31) - itself; otherwise `destroyer`. **Not a ship**: not is_land (+0x2D), or a combat_width (+0xE8) of 0 or less, or the `hq_brigade` - itself; softness (+0x124) under g_AiAirNavalPowerBase - `armor_brigade`; canParadrop (+0x38) set, or the `bergsjaeger_brigade` or `marine_brigade` - itself; otherwise `infantry_brigade`. So an aircraft is always its own group. Callers: CCountry::CountMaxUnitsStillBuildable (twice, the type and each brigade) and CUnit::UpdatePlanForceNeeds (the `GenericType` its record describes). The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x5ADF70-0x5AE004 read whole: `mov eax,[edx+0x1c]; mov ecx,[eax+esi*4]`, then the tests on +0x2E, +0x190, the db's +0xA0/+0x98/+0xA8/+0xAC (heavy_cruiser, battleship, destroyer, carrier), +0x2F, +0x30, +0x31, +0x2D, +0xE8, db+0x78 (hq_brigade), +0x124 against [0x1A886AC] (g_AiAirNavalPowerBase), +0x38, db+0x40/+0x44 (bergsjaeger, marine), db+0x2C (armor) and db+0x34 (infantry), each answered as `mov eax,[x+0x24]; ret`. The callers set ESI to a type_index and EDX to CSubUnitDataBase::GetInstance() at 0x4E145F-0x4E146C and 0x4E14A8-0x4E14B2. Wrong if a caller passes something else in ESI.

addresses.name: CCountry::CountMaxUnitsStillBuildable
addresses.comment: **How many more brigades of a unit type the country may have.** The game's own name, out of the Lua API; `ret 4`. Answers **0** when technology_status->unit_available (+0x27C) has the type clear, when SubUnitDefinitionIsUsableBy(the technology status's country's tag, definition) says no, or when the type has an available_trigger (+0x1D0 set) that is false for an event scope of the country. Answers **1,000,000** when minimum_of_type (+0x1B8, a plain count) and max_percentage_of_type (+0x1BC, thousandths) are both under 1 - every type with no cap. Otherwise, with group = SubUnitTypeGroup(type): `all` = the brigades of the country's units (+0xBAC) whose own type folds to the same group; `have` = the brigades of exactly this type in those units, **plus line->Size for every brigade of this type in every military line of the queue** (a line of two such brigades and a series of 3 adds 6), plus each brigade of this type in a unit waiting to be placed (a CUnitDeployment, slot 8 = 0x4B4). Answer `max(minimum_of_type - have, all * max_percentage_of_type / 1000 - have)` (the second truncated, through `all*1000*pct/1000` then `/1000`), and 0 where that is 0 or less. **`all` counts the map only**: the queue and the units waiting add to `have` but not to `all`. Callers: the four builder lists, CanBuildDivision, CBrigadeBuilder::Update and the Lua `GetEliteUnitBuildCount`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md, section 2, and FINDINGS-ministers.md, section C.
addresses.revises: Raised from inferred: read whole on the listing. Adds that `all` counts only units on the map, that a queued line counts every brigade of the type times its Size, what groups the types (SubUnitTypeGroup, 0x1ADF70), the scales of the two keys (minimum_of_type a count by atoi, max_percentage_of_type thousandths by TokenToFixedPoint) and the truncation.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x4E13A0-0x4E15D7: unit_available `cmp byte [ecx+edx],0` at 0x4E13C0; SubUnitDefinitionIsUsableBy at 0x4E13D8 with ecx = [[edi+0xDF8]+0x248]+0xCA4; the trigger at 0x4E142A; `mov eax,0xF4240` at 0x4E144C after both caps tested `jg`; the units walk 0x4E148D-0x4E14D6 adding 1 to [esp+0x1C] (all) when SubUnitTypeGroup matches and to [esp+0x10] (have) when the index also matches; the queue walk 0x4E14F0-0x4E152A `add edi,[esi+0x40]` per matching brigade; the deployment walk 0x4E1540-0x4E1588 `inc edi`; the arithmetic 0x4E158A-0x4E15D2. The loader stores +0x1B8 from atoi (0x5A4C3B) and +0x1BC from TokenToFixedPoint (0x5A4C5D). Wrong if the unit list at +0xBAC is not every unit the country owns.

addresses.name: CCountry::UpdateManpowerAfterMobilising
addresses.comment: **Works out CCountry +0x158, the manpower the country has to spare once every brigade is refilled - which is what the Lua `HasExtraManpowerLeft` tests above 0.** `country` on the stack, `ret 4` at 0x4DD057. In order, all thousandths and every divide truncating: `+0x158 = manpower (+0xBCC)`; then `+= max_manpower (+0xBD0) * 1000 / (1000 + values[GLOBAL_MANPOWER] (modifier 6, +0x30) + floor(technology_status->manpower_gain (+0x8C) rounded to thousandths through a float)) * 1000 / MAX_MANPOWER * 1000 / 2000` - half a year's manpower before its multipliers; then for every unit of +0xBAC with reinforcements_active (+0xA6), every brigade: `short = (max_strength - strength) * 1000 / max_strength` (-1 where max_strength is 0), `-= (short + 250) * build_cost_manpower (+0xFC) / 1000` - the men it lacks **plus a quarter of what it takes to build**, 250 being g at 0x1A87470, floor(250.5f) set by a static initialiser; then for every military line with is_reserve (+0x8C), every brigade definition once (not times the line's Size): `-= ((1000 + RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE (+0x268)) * max_strength / 1000) * build_cost_manpower / 1000 * 1000 / max_strength` - the men of the strength a reserve brigade is built at. Five callers: **RunCountryDailyPass at 0x4DBEA3, every day for every country**, CConstructUnitCommand::Execute (0x5461B7), CConstructSingleUnitCommand::Execute (0x547229), the upgrade command at 0x5DA7C0 (0x5DAE81) and CInGameIdler::Enter (0x65B7CA). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ministers.md, section C.
addresses.revises: Read whole (the record had it read in part, with no signature and its `ret` not reached): adds the signature, the half-year term's arithmetic, the quarter-brigade headroom constant, the reserve-line term (the built strength's men, once per brigade) and the daily caller in RunCountryDailyPass, which the record's caller list lacked.

Wrong if MAX_MANPOWER is not the first dword of the military block.

addresses.name: CCountry::HasExtraManpowerLeft
addresses.comment: The Lua `HasExtraManpowerLeft`: `+0x158 > 0`, signed. +0x158 is what CCountry::UpdateManpowerAfterMobilising (0xDCD70) leaves there - the pool plus half a year's manpower less what refilling every brigade (and a quarter of each brigade's build manpower) and the reserve lines would take - refreshed daily in RunCountryDailyPass and after an order. addresses.name: CCountry::GetICPart
addresses.signature: CFixedPoint* __thiscall CCountry::GetICPart(CCountry* this, CFixedPoint* out, int category)
addresses.comment: **The IC one production share has, in thousandths.** `setting = ProductionDistribution[category]` (the vector at +0x5F4, in ProductionCategory order: 0 lend-lease, 1 consumer goods, 2 production, 3 supply, 4 reinforcement, 5 upgrade - no bounds check); then in 48.15 fixed point `((TotalIC << 15) * base_percentage >> 15) * factor >> 15`, and that times `1000 << 15` shifted right 30. TotalIC (+0x604) is **whole IC**, so the answer is `TotalIC * base_percentage * factor` in thousandths, each shift flooring. It is the share's slider times the whole IC, not what the share was paid or needs. `ret 8`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ministers.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x503D10-0x503D7E: `mov eax,[ecx+0x5F4]; mov esi,[eax+edx*4]`; `mov eax,[ecx+0x604]; cdq; shld edx,eax,0xF; shl eax,0xF`; __allmul with [esi+8]/[esi+0xC], `shrd 0xF`; __allmul with [esi+0x10]/[esi+0x14], `shrd 0xF`; __allmul with 0x1F40000, `shrd 0x1E`; `ret 8`. addresses.no_signature: A pointer-to-virtual-member thunk: `mov eax,[ecx]; jmp [eax+0x48]` - it has the signature of whatever slot 18 of the receiver's table is, which differs between its claimants.

addresses.name: CConstructUnitCommand::CConstructUnitCommand
addresses.signature: CConstructUnitCommand* __stdcall CConstructUnitCommand::CConstructUnitCommand(CConstructUnitCommand* this, void* brigades, int province, int amount, bool reserve, bool buildNow, CCountryTag country, CCountryTag builder, CID target) @EAX
addresses.comment: **The constructor every poster uses** - the four builder windows, the licence action, the production screen and the Lua `CConstructUnitCommand(...)`. Everything on the stack, `this` first, `ret 0x30`. CCommand's base (class id 0x18D, type ids 0x2D7 `buildunit`, +0x34 = 0xFFFF); country -> +0x3C/+0x40, builder -> +0x44/+0x48, province -> +0x4C, amount -> +0x70, reserve -> +0x74 (byte), target -> +0x78/+0x7C, buildNow -> +0x80 (byte). **Mints three kinds of number** under the spin lock at 0x1B16714, as the building and convoy commands do: the line's id (type `0x1268 + word[0x1A857EC]`, serial counter + 1) into +0x50/+0x54; the unit's into +0x58/+0x5C, the counter then moving on by `1 + 2 * amount`; and for each brigade of the list (`brigades`, a CList<CSubUnitDefinition const*>, in its order) a new CBrigadeConstructionDefinition (0x54 bytes: the command's country at +8, its own id with the counter moving by `1 + amount`, the type at +0x34) appended to +0x60, whose model list (+0x44) is given, for each technology of the type in the type's order (+0x44..+0x48), **the builder's level of it** - the country's where the builder's id is 0 - and, where the builder is the country itself and is a government in exile, the higher of that and its faction's first member's level. Nothing is refused or tested here. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ministers.md, section C.

addresses.name: LuaConstruct_CConstructUnitCommand
addresses.signature: void __stdcall LuaConstruct_CConstructUnitCommand(void* self_argument, void* brigades, int province, int amount, bool reserve, CCountryTag country, CCountryTag builder, CID target)
addresses.comment: **Lua `CConstructUnitCommand(tag, list, province, count, reserve, builder, target)`** (luabind's `__init(argument, CCountryTag, CList<const CSubUnitDefinition*>&, int, int, bool, CCountryTag, CID)`; luabind's layout puts the plain arguments first and the by-value classes after, in their order): news 0x84 bytes and calls CConstructUnitCommand::CConstructUnitCommand(list, province, count, reserve, **buildNow 0**, the first tag as the country, the second as the builder, the CID as the target), then wraps it in a luabind pointer holder (vftable 0x15F21DC). So a script's order is always queued, never built at once. **Constructing it mints the line's, the unit's and the brigades' numbers** whether or not the script posts it. `ret 0x2C`. One caller, the invoker 0x97C9D0. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ministers.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x988E90-0x988F91: `push 0x84; call new`; pushes [ebp+0x2C]/[ebp+0x30] (copied), [ebp+0x28], [ebp+0x24], [ebp+0x20], [ebp+0x1C], ebx = 0, [ebp+0x18], [ebp+0x14], [ebp+0x10], [ebp+0xC], the object; `call 0x545760`; holder vftable 0x15F21DC at 0x988F57; `ret 0x2C`. That the first tag is the country is borne out by the April 1936 save: every AI line (id type 4713) is in its own country's queue with country = its own tag and builder = its own tag (the null tag's id 0 falling back to the country), none with a target.

addresses.name: LuabindInvoke_CConstructUnitCommand_Init
addresses.signature: int __cdecl LuabindInvoke_CConstructUnitCommand_Init(void* function@stack:4, void* context@stack:8, lua_State* L@EAX) @EAX
addresses.comment: luabind's overload test and call for `CConstructUnitCommand.__init`. Seven arguments after the class table, matched against `lua_gettop`: the two tags through the tag converter 0x98C7D0, the list through the class lookup 0xB7E650 (a SubUnitList object, by reference), the province and the count each `lua_type == LUA_TNUMBER`, the reserve `lua_type == LUA_TBOOLEAN`, the CID through 0x98CF60. A wrong type for any of them is a luabind 'no matching overload' error in the script, not a refused command. Bare `ret`, the callers clean. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ministers.md, section C.

addresses.name: LuaConstruct_SubUnitList
addresses.no_signature: luabind's construct thunk for a class with no arguments: the luabind::argument arrives in EAX, nothing on the stack, bare `ret`.
addresses.comment: **Lua `SubUnitList()`**: news a 0x10-byte CList<CSubUnitDefinition const*> - first, last and count zero, the byte zero - and wraps it in a luabind holder (vftable 0x15F222C). An empty list; `SubUnitList.Append` fills it. One caller, 0x97DF49. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ministers.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x989340-0x9893C4: `push 0x10; call new`, stores of 0 to +0, +4, +8 and the byte +0xC, holder vftable 0x15F222C; bare `ret`. luabind.json gives SubUnitList's one constructor as `__init(argument)` with size 16.

addresses.name: AppendSubUnit
addresses.comment: The Lua `SubUnitList.Append(list, type)`: appends a 0x10-byte node {definition, prev, next, byte} at the list's tail and adds 1 to its count. **No test of the definition**: a nil (an unknown name from GetSubUnit) goes in as a null node, which the command's constructor would read through. Bare `ret`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ministers.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x8EAC10-0x8EAC5C: `push 0x10; call new`, the node filled from [ebp+0xC] and the old tail [esi+4], `inc` of [esi+8], the head set when the count was 0, otherwise the old tail's +8. No compare of [ebp+0xC]. One luabind registration (the name is the same).

addresses.name: CArray4_GetAt
addresses.signature: void* __stdcall CArray4_GetAt(void* array@ECX, unsigned int index@stack:4) @EAX
addresses.comment: `&data[index]` for an array of four-byte elements: `[ecx] + index * 4`, **no bounds check**, index from 0. Registered as GetAt of CArray<int>, CArray<CFixedPoint> and CArray<float>, so it is recorded class-free (trap 4). An index past the end reads whatever lies there. `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x8F1330-0x8F133C: `mov eax,[ecx]; mov ecx,[ebp+8]; lea eax,[eax+ecx*4]; ret 4`. luabind.json: three registrations, no vftable.

addresses.name: CArray4_GetSize
addresses.comment: `(end - begin) >> 2`: the count of a four-byte-element array whose begin is at +0 and end at +4. Registered as GetSize of CArray<int>, CArray<CFixedPoint> and CArray<float>, so recorded class-free. Bare `ret`.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x421320-0x421328: `mov eax,[ecx+4]; sub eax,[ecx]; sar eax,2; ret`. luabind.json: three registrations, no vftable.

addresses.name: CArrayInt_SetAt
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CArrayInt_SetAt(void* array@ECX, unsigned int index@stack:4, int* value@stack:8)
addresses.comment: The Lua `CArrayInt:SetAt(i, v)`: `data[index] = *value`, no bounds check, index from 0. `ret 8`.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x8F12F0-0x8F1301: `mov eax,[ecx]; mov ecx,[ebp+0xC]; mov edx,[ecx]; mov ecx,[ebp+8]; mov [eax+ecx*4],edx; ret 8`. One luabind registration (CArray<int>::SetAt), no vftable.

structs.name: CConstructUnitCommand
structs.comment: The order for a unit line. Made by CConstructUnitCommand::CConstructUnitCommand (0x145760); Execute is slot 6, IsValid slot 14. Allocated 0x84 bytes by every poster (the Lua constructor 0x988E90, the builder windows, the licence action).
structs.evidence: `push 0x84` before the constructor at 0x988ED5 and in the licence action; the constructor writes vftable 0x15C3654 (rva 0x11C3654), which vtable.py lists as CConstructUnitCommand's table at object offset 0; the constructor writes the CCommand base fields (+0x4 class id 0x18D, +0x2C/+0x30 type ids, +0x34) at the offsets CCommand's record has.

struct_fields.name: country
struct_fields.comment: Whose queue the line goes into: Execute takes the country as countries[+0x40]. The Lua constructor's first tag.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor 0x5457DB-0x5457E7 from [ebp+0x20]/[ebp+0x24]; Execute's `countries_first[this+0x40]`.

struct_fields.name: builder
struct_fields.comment: Who builds it. Where its id (+0x48) is 0 - the Lua CNullTag() - Execute and the constructor use the country instead. Saved as `builder`. A licence sets the seller here.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor 0x5457DE/0x5457FB-0x5457FE from [ebp+0x28]/[ebp+0x2C]; the `cmp eax,ebx; jne` on +0x48 at 0x54586E; Execute's `if (this+0x48 == 0)` fallback. fieldmap: the save key `builder` lands at +0x44/+0x48.

struct_fields.name: province
struct_fields.comment: A province id. **Execute only copies provinces[id] into the line's location, which CCountry::EnqueueConstruction then zeroes** - so on the ordinary path it is never used, nothing tests it against the country, and an id of 0 or one the country does not hold changes nothing. Only the build-now path (never from Lua) keeps it.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor `mov [edi+0x4C],eax` from [ebp+0x10]; Execute's `provinces_begin[this+0x4C]` stored to location; EnqueueConstruction's record (zeroes +0x44). The April 1936 save: no military line has a location.

struct_fields.name: line_id_type
struct_fields.comment: Type half of the line's id, `0x1268 + word[0x1A857EC]` (4713 in the maintainer's saves); Execute gives it to the line through SetId.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor 0x545806-0x545820.

struct_fields.name: line_id
struct_fields.comment: The line's serial, the counter at 0x1A857F8 plus 1.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor 0x54580D-0x545823.

struct_fields.name: unit_id_type
struct_fields.comment: Type half of the number the unit will take; the line's unit_type.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor's second mint; Execute copies it to CMilitaryConstruction +0x58.

struct_fields.name: unit_id
struct_fields.comment: The number the unit will take; the counter then moves on by 1 + 2 x amount.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor's second mint (`counter + 1 + amount * 2`); Execute copies it to CMilitaryConstruction +0x5C.

struct_fields.name: brigades
struct_fields.comment: One CBrigadeConstructionDefinition for each entry of the list the poster gave, in its order, each with the builder's technology levels as its model. The count (+0x68) is what IsValid asks; Execute gives each to the line with CMilitaryConstruction::AddBrigade and names the unit only where there is more than one.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor's append loop (head +0x60, tail +0x64, count +0x68, byte +0x6C zeroed at 0x54582B-0x54583A); IsValid `cmp [ecx+0x68],0`; Execute's `if (1 < this+0x68)` around MakeUnitName.

struct_fields.name: amount
struct_fields.comment: The line's Size: how many units of it are built **one after another** - a series, not lines side by side. Execute takes every unit's men at once (amount x each brigade's men). Not tested: 0 makes a line that still builds one unit, takes no men and counts nothing in ProductionSubUnitCounts.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor from [ebp+0x14]; Execute `pCVar9->Size = this+0x70` and the men `floor((amount + 0.0005) * 1000) * men / 1000`; CMilitaryConstruction::Deliver's `size -= 1; return size <= 0`. The April 1936 save: AI lines of size 1 to 4.

struct_fields.name: is_reserve
struct_fields.comment: Copied to the line's is_reserve, which gives it reserves_factor (slot 8) and charges RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE on its IC and men.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor `mov [edi+0x74],al` from byte [ebp+0x18]; Execute's `is_reserve = this+0x74` and the reserve term of the men.

struct_fields.name: target_type
struct_fields.comment: Type half of the object the line is aimed at; 0 from the Lua CID().
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor from [ebp+0x30]; Execute copies to CMilitaryConstruction +0x90.

struct_fields.name: target_id
struct_fields.comment: The object the line is aimed at; 0 for none, and then the finished unit waits to be placed.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor from [ebp+0x34]; Execute copies to CMilitaryConstruction +0x94.

struct_fields.name: build_now
struct_fields.comment: Build it at once instead of queueing it (FINDINGS-production.md). Always 0 from Lua.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor `mov [edi+0x80],al` from byte [ebp+0x1C]; the Lua constructor pushes 0 for it (0x988F1A).

struct_fields.name: DeployedSubUnitCounts
struct_fields.comment: The game's own name for it, out of the Lua API (`GetDeployedSubUnitCounts`, rva 0x4E8180, `lea eax,[ecx+0xE8]`). **Per type_index, the country's brigades of that type**: one for every brigade of every unit in CCountry +0xBAC and of every unit waiting to be placed. Sized to the number of unit types by the constructor and filled only by CEU3AI::UpdateSubUnitCounts (0x499770), every day at the production minister's hour, just before ProductionMinister_Tick.
struct_fields.revises: Adds what it counts and who fills it, when.
struct_fields.evidence: CEU3AI::UpdateSubUnitCounts 0x899874-0x899913; the constructor 0x888020 grows it to (db+0x20-db+0x1C)/4 zeroed entries; no other writer found by a disp32 scan.

struct_fields.name: ProductionSubUnitCounts
struct_fields.comment: The game's own name for it, out of the Lua API (`GetProductionSubUnitCounts`, rva 0x4E8190, `lea eax,[ecx+0xF8]`). **Per type_index, the brigades of that type still to come out of the queue**: each brigade of each military line counted times the line's Size (the units of its series not yet delivered). Filled only by CEU3AI::UpdateSubUnitCounts (0x499770), daily at the production minister's hour.
struct_fields.revises: Adds what it counts and who fills it, when.
struct_fields.evidence: CEU3AI::UpdateSubUnitCounts 0x899826-0x89986F: `add [edx+ecx*4], [esi+0x40]` per brigade of each line whose slot 17 answers true.

struct_fields.name: TheatreSubUnitNeedCounts
struct_fields.comment: The game's own name for it, out of the Lua API (`GetTheatreSubUnitNeedCounts`, rva 0x3918C0). Per type_index, the sum over the AI's unit agents of their unit's plan_subunit_group_difference (CUnit +0x6C), floored at 0 after each agent; the transport_ship type left out where all the country's areas are landlocked. Filled by CEU3AI::UpdateSubUnitCounts (0x499770). TFH's production script has its read commented out.
struct_fields.revises: Adds what it counts and who fills it.
struct_fields.evidence: CEU3AI::UpdateSubUnitCounts 0x899937-0x8999E7, slot 74 of the agent (ReturnDwordAt0x64, the agent's CUnit) and its +0x6C/+0x70 vector.

struct_fields.name: hasFilledProdQueue
struct_fields.comment: The game's own name for it, out of the Lua API (`HasFilledProdQueue`, rva 0x4E8170). Set to 1 by CEU3AI::UpdateSubUnitCounts (0x499770) as it finishes - so it means the counts have been worked out at least once.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov byte ptr [ebx+0xAA],1` at 0x8999F1.

struct_fields.name: Escorts
struct_fields.comment: The game's own name for it, out of the Lua API (`GetEscorts`, rva 0x17C30). **The escorts on no convoy**, saved as `escorts`: a finished escort line adds CONVOY_CONSTRUCTION_SIZE here (CConvoyConstruction::Deliver) and CCountry::DistributeConvoyShips hands them out and takes them back each day. Escorts sitting on convoys are not counted - at war, those a convoy was given; at peace none are wanted and all come back here.
struct_fields.revises: Adds that it is the free pool only, and its writers.
struct_fields.evidence: DistributeConvoyShips 0x4FD7BC (escortsOwned starts from it), 0x4FDE59-0x4FDE9D (escorts given back added to it); CConvoyConstruction::Deliver's record.

struct_fields.name: TotalConvoyTransports
struct_fields.comment: The game's own name for it, out of the Lua API (`GetTotalConvoyTransports`, rva 0x4E8200). **Every transport the country has**: the free ones (+0xB0, `Transports`) plus each convoy's (CConvoy +0x98), worked out by CCountry::DistributeConvoyShips at the start of its pass - so it is as of the day's sharing out, before anything a later convoy order adds.
struct_fields.revises: Adds what it sums and its one writer in play.
struct_fields.evidence: DistributeConvoyShips 0x4FD76F-0x4FD77F (`[+0xBC] = [+0xB0]`) and 0x4FD7DE-0x4FD7E4 (`add [ebx+0xBC], [edi+0x98]` per convoy).

struct_fields.name: TotalNeededConvoyTransports
struct_fields.comment: The game's own name for it, out of the Lua API (`GetTotalNeededConvoyTransports`, rva 0x4E8210). **The transports already on convoys, as they stood before the day's sharing, plus TotalNeededTransports (+0xB8)** - the transports_wanted of every convoy that is not idle. Worked out by CCountry::DistributeConvoyShips. So `needed - total` is `wanted - free`: the script's `liNeeded - liCurrent` is the shortfall of the free pool against what the convoys want, not the convoys' own shortfall.
struct_fields.revises: Adds what it sums, and that it counts the convoys' transports as well as their wants.
struct_fields.evidence: DistributeConvoyShips 0x4FD785 (zeroed), 0x4FD7EA-0x4FD7F0 (`add [ebx+0xC0], [edi+0x98]` per convoy, beside the +0xBC sum) and 0x4FDEB5-0x4FDEBB (`add [ebx+0xC0], [ebx+0xB8]`) after steps 5 and 6 summed the wants into +0xB8 (FINDINGS-supplyconvoys.md section 7).

struct_fields.name: starting_manpower
struct_fields.comment: LoadKey copies Manpower into this the moment it has read the `manpower` key. **Its real meaning is the second writer's, and the name does not fit it**: CCountry::UpdateManpowerAfterMobilising (0xDCD70), run every day in RunCountryDailyPass and after every unit order, sets it to the manpower pool plus half a year's manpower before its multipliers, less the men every reinforcing brigade lacks plus a quarter of each one's build manpower, less the built-strength men of each brigade of a reserve line. Its reader is the Lua `HasExtraManpowerLeft` (rva 0x4E81E0, `> 0`). The name is kept because BiceLib's CCountry.hpp uses it; `spare_manpower` is what it is.
struct_fields.revises: Adds the full arithmetic, the daily writer, and its reader; name and type unchanged.
struct_fields.evidence: CCountry::UpdateManpowerAfterMobilising read whole (0x4DCD70-0x4DD057); HasExtraManpowerLeft 0x8E81E0 `cmp [ecx+0x158],0; setg al`; findRefs --callers 0x4DCD70 includes 0x4DBEA3 in RunCountryDailyPass.

struct_fields.name: is_land
struct_fields.comment: **`type = land`** in the type's file. The Lua `IsRegiment` (rva 0x62D10, `mov al,[ecx+0x2D]`) answers this byte - so to the script every land type is a 'regiment', and TFH's CreateUnit builds every land type as reserves in peacetime. CMilitaryConstruction::IsLand asks it of a line's first brigade.
struct_fields.revises: Raised from a name inferred off one consumer to the loader's own store; adds the Lua IsRegiment reading it.
struct_fields.evidence: CSubUnitDefinition::LoadKey: key token 0xD9 (`type`) with value 0x442 (`land`) - `mov byte ptr [edi+0x2D],1` at 0x5A3DAE; 0x443 (`naval`) at 0x5A3DD0 to +0x2E; 0x440 (`air`) at 0x5A3DF6 to +0x2C (token names from saveTokens.py).

struct_fields.name: is_ship
struct_fields.comment: **`type = naval`** in the type's file. CMilitaryConstruction::IsNaval asks it of a line's first brigade; SubUnitTypeGroup folds ships on it.
struct_fields.revises: The record said `unknown`: adds the key that sets it.
struct_fields.evidence: CSubUnitDefinition::LoadKey 0x5A3DC9-0x5A3DD0: `cmp eax,0x443` (`naval`) then `mov byte ptr [edi+0x2E],1`.

struct_fields.name: is_cag
struct_fields.comment: **`is_cag = yes`** in the type's file (TFH: `cag` alone). The Lua `IsCag` (rva 0xC8350) answers it; the production script counts an air line whose first brigade has it as naval IC.
struct_fields.revises: Raised from inferred-by-position to the loader's store.
struct_fields.evidence: fieldmap.py CSubUnitDefinition: `is_cag 0x521 +0x32 byte`; LoadKey 0x5A4492-0x5A44A5 tests the value against 0x1F6 (`yes`) and stores 1; IsCag 0x4C8350 `mov al,[ecx+0x32]`.

struct_fields.name: minimum_of_type
struct_fields.comment: The `minimum_of_type` key, **a plain count** (atoi, not thousandths): TFH gives 6 to its five elite brigades. Read by CCountry::CountMaxUnitsStillBuildable, which lets the country have at least this many brigades of the type.
struct_fields.revises: Adds its scale and its consumer.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadKey 0x5A4C31-0x5A4C40: `call 0xB969F1` (atoi) on the token, stored to +0x1B8; CountMaxUnitsStillBuildable 0x4E1430 and 0x4E15A6.

struct_fields.name: max_percentage_of_type
struct_fields.comment: The `max_percentage_of_type` key, **thousandths** (TokenToFixedPoint: 0.04 is 40). Read by CCountry::CountMaxUnitsStillBuildable: the type may make up this share of the country's brigades of its group on the map.
struct_fields.revises: Adds its scale and its consumer.
struct_fields.evidence: LoadKey 0x5A4C4B-0x5A4C64: TokenToFixedPoint (0xA69550) on parse+0x228, stored to +0x1BC; CountMaxUnitsStillBuildable 0x4E1436 and 0x4E1594.
